key_insight: SCE-SLAM uses learned scene-coordinate embeddings as a global, metric anchor inside a monocular SLAM pipeline to prevent scale drift across long sequences while preserving real-time local optimization.
problem_solved: Monocular SLAM systems accumulate scale drift over long videos because local frame-to-frame optimization lacks global metric constraints; SCE-SLAM enforces a consistent global scale across independent optimization windows.
method: Learn per-pixel / per-keypoint scene coordinate embeddings that map image observations to a shared metric 3D coordinate space.
Integrate embedding-based global constraints into an end-to-end SLAM pipeline so local windowed optimizers are anchored to a consistent scale and can be globally aligned.
Maintain real-time performance by combining lightweight local optimization with occasional global consistency updates via embedding matches (no heavy full-batch bundle adjustment).
impact: Provides reliable, scale-consistent monocular 3D reconstruction suitable for long-range mapping, internet-video reconstruction, and resource-constrained robotics — reducing post-processing and improving downstream perception tasks.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: image -> scene-coordinate embedding network -> embedding matches -> SLAM optimizer (local windows + global anchor).
Before/after scale drift plot: trajectory or scale factor drift over time for baseline monocular SLAM vs SCE-SLAM.
Heatmap overlay on frames showing predicted scene coordinates (colors map to metric depth/position).
Comparison table/chart of qualitative outcomes (reconstructed map snippets) showing consistent scale vs warped scale.
paper_title: SCE-SLAM: Scale-Consistent Monocular SLAM via Scene Coordinate Embeddings
paper_authors: Yuchen Wu, Jiahe Li, Xiaohan Yu, Lina Yu, Jin Zheng
